A trigger advances the simulation by one frame, in place of the internal clock.

Starts and stops the simulation; the space bar does the same.
Advances the simulation by one frame on each press.

lines: Maps one parameter of another module onto four separate knobs, so several controllers can drive that parameter at once.
Binds a parameter to this group of four knobs: press it, then click a knob, fader or switch on any module.

Menu — Read — on a knob's own right-click menu, or by double-clicking that knob; switched off, the knob sends its value out and ignores changes made to the parameter elsewhere.
Menu — Audio rate processing — switched off, the mapped parameter is updated every 32nd sample instead of every sample.
Note — the four knobs do nothing until the mapping button is pressed and a knob, fader or switch on another module is clicked.
Morphs the parameters of other modules between up to twelve snapshots, fading from one to the next over a set time.
Short-press applies this snapshot to the bound parameters, or in write mode stores their current values into it; long-press clears it, or sets the sequence length in read mode.
Read morphs between snapshots as the CV input selects them, Auto stores the current values whenever a new snapshot is selected, and Write stores them into the snapshot pressed.
Sets how long a fade between snapshots takes, about 10ms at the bottom of its travel and about 10 seconds at the top, on an exponential curve.
Sets the curve of the fade: linear at the centre, easing in on one side and easing out on the other.
Adds to the fade time set by the knob or by the snapshot, one volt counting as a tenth of the knob's travel.
Selects the snapshot: a trigger steps through the slots forward, reverse, ping-pong, at random or shuffled, 0-10V or a note picks one outright, and Phase mode scans through them.
A trigger restarts the snapshot sequence at the first usable slot.
Carries a rising envelope during a fade, a gate while one runs, a trigger on a snapshot change or at the start or end of a fade, or all of these on separate polyphonic channels.
Menu — Bind module (left) — binds every parameter of the module on the left; Bind module (select), Bind single parameter, Bind multiple parameters and Bind parameters by selection bind chosen ones.
Menu — Set as first and Set as last — on a snapshot button's own right-click menu, narrowing the range of slots used for sequencing and for CV selection.
Menu — Clamp Fade CV input — switched off, the fade CV can push the fade time past ten seconds, as far as several hours.
Menu — Port CV mode — the Trigger modes step through the snapshots, 0..10V and C4 pick one outright, Arm applies one on the next clock trigger, Phase scans through them, and Off ignores the port.
Menu — Port OUT mode — Envelope, Gate, Trigger snapshot change, Trigger fade start, Trigger fade end, Polyphonic, Phase or Tipsy.
Menu — Snapshots — sets which slots the sequence runs over, with Set by long-press switching the long-press shortcut for it on and off.
Menu — Precision — morphs at the audio rate, or at an eighth, a sixty-fourth, a two hundred and fifty-sixth or a thousand and twenty-fourth of it, for less CPU.
Menu — Bound modules and Bound parameters — list what is bound, each parameter carrying Locate and indicate and Unbind; Clean invalid parameters up drops the ones whose module has gone.
Menu — Fade — on a snapshot button's own right-click menu: Parameter/CV takes the fade time from the FADE knob and its CV, and Custom gives that snapshot a fade time of its own.
Menu — Save, Load, Clear, Copy, Paste, Randomize and save, Shift front, Shift back, Custom label and Custom color — on a snapshot button's own right-click menu.
Menu — Hide mapping indicators — stops the pink square being drawn beside each bound parameter.
Note — fifteen +T expanders to the right raise the total number of snapshots to 192.
Note — nothing morphs until parameters are bound from the context menu and snapshots have been stored: flip the switch to W, set the parameters, and short-press a snapshot button.
Transit.notes: The manual calls the fade-clamp option Disable CV clamping; the installed v2.5.0 source has it as Clamp Fade CV input, with the sense reversed. The item name here follows the source. In C4 mode a second channel on the same cable triggers the load, so there the jack reads two channels of a polyphonic cable. PHASE is the one mode that reads the voltage continuously rather than as a step.
